messages.subject: measurement invariance and chi-square difference test
parts:
Hi 

The chi-square difference suggest that the model does not hold up even at the weak invariance level, but the CFI cut off is below 0.01 (Hirschfeld, von Brachel, 2014), suggesting that it is fine.  Which should I follow? 

I would appreciate some help! 
Thank you!

messages.author: af82fa98896529e2
messages.subject: Re: measurement invariance and chi-square difference test
parts: I do not think this is the lavaan question. The likelihood-ratio test is sensitive to sample size like chi-square of absolute fit. The change in CFI is used to fix this problem. However, experts have different opinions on this index and the use of fit indices in general. To be honest, it depends on the reviewers of your paper.
